sermon.title: Guard Your Heart
sermon.speaker: Speaker at Vine Cluster Church (name not given in the recording)
sermon.summary: In this message a speaker at Vine Cluster Church teaches Proverbs 4:23, “above all else guard your heart,” and says what we take in is what comes out. He compares Israel’s request for a king, Saul’s disobedience, David’s heart after God and Solomon’s turned heart. He closes with Romans 8 and Philippians 4:8 and the choice of which side, the flesh or the spirit, we feed.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. The recording does not give the speaker’s name, and it is not stated whether he is Pastor Kincer or a guest (he gives the same freeway illustration as in “Learning and Following What the Bible Says”). Editor notes: “Bathsheba” and “reign” are caption corrections; several garbled words are marked [unclear] (“the [unclear] few weeks ago,” “back to the [unclear],” “[unclear] so you just as well,” “big and tough and [unclear],” “this other [unclear]”). He reads from a modern translation, so wording differs from the NKJV shown; he says “1 Kings chapter 3… verse 9,” and gives Romans 8:5–6 as “8 and 5… verse 86.” He says Solomon became king “when he was 20 years old” and that Saul reigned “42 years,” which are his own figures and not verified here; Acts 13:21 gives 40 years for Saul’s reign. He says God could “raise up a country as small as mexico” to overthrow the United States, and gives opinions about picking a spouse; these are his own views. He mentions a coworker and an elderly woman without naming them.

chunks.section_question: What does Proverbs 4:23 mean when it says to “guard your heart”?
chunks.short_answer: He says “guard your heart for everything you do flows from it,” and that in the chapter Solomon passes on what his father taught him: get wisdom, hold on to instruction and stay off “the path of the wicked.” He says “the path of the righteous is straight and full of light,” while evildoers “stumble in the darkness.”

chunks.section_question: What is the battle between the flesh and the spirit, and which side wins?
chunks.short_answer: He says “the one that gets stronger is the one we feed,” so feeding the flesh will “eventually put out the spiritual side,” while feeding the spiritual side makes it “stronger and stronger.” He says coming to praise Jesus “charges your batteries,” and “if you don’t charge your batteries you’re not going to function spiritually.”

chunks.section_question: What does the bulletproof vest illustrate about guarding the heart?
chunks.short_answer: He describes a vest with a pocket for a card covering the heart, saying “from a spiritual standpoint” we need protection too, because “if it gets a direct hit… you’re going to die spiritually.” He says “we have to always be on guard what we take in because what we take in is what’s going to come out.”

chunks.section_question: Why did nations fear Israel, and why does he say going against God is “suicidal”?

And to one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one, to each according to his own ability; and immediately he went on a journey. After a long time the lord of those servants came and settled accounts with them. “So he who had received five talents came and brought five other talents, saying, ‘Lord, you delivered to me five talents; look, I have gained five more talents besides them.’ His lord said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant; you were faithful over a few things, I will make you ruler over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord.’ He also who had received two talents came and said, ‘Lord, you delivered to me two talents; look, I have gained two more talents besides them.’ His lord said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant; you have been faithful over a few things, I will make you ruler over many things. And I was afraid, and went and hid your talent in the ground. Look, there you have what is yours.’ “But his lord answered and said to him, ‘You wicked and lazy servant, you knew that I reap where I have not sown, and gather where I have not scattered seed. faqs.question: What story does he tell about a coworker who could not stop cussing?
faqs.answer: He says a man told him he was a Christian but “can’t stop cussing,” and he told him “the problem is not your mouth the problem is your heart,” since “what comes out of your mouth comes out of your heart.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: But those things which proceed out of the mouth come from the heart, and they defile a man.

faqs.question: Does he say God takes us back when we fail?
faqs.answer: Yes. He says “no matter what we do in this life if we are willing God will take us back… sometimes we’ll stumble sometimes we’ll fall,” but we need “a heart that’s willing to follow Jesus.”

faqs.question: Does he say the battle in the mind ever stops?
faqs.answer: No. He says “I don’t care if you’ve served God for five minutes or five years it still happens even if you served him for decades,” because the fleshly side “still rises up within you once in a while.”

faqs.question: How does he compare Israel’s invisible king with ours?
faqs.answer: He says “we have this king but nobody can see him but we can feel his presence,” and that other nations asked “where’s your king” and Israel’s answer was that “our king’s God.”

faqs.question: What does he say happened to Egypt?
faqs.answer: He says “that country was almost destroyed” because of Pharaoh’s “hardness of heart” and that “it cost him economically.”

faqs.question: What does he say God could do to a powerful nation?
faqs.answer: He says “God if he wanted to he could raise up a country as small as mexico and he could overthrow the united states of America,” and that “that’s how powerful our God is.”

faqs.question: What does he say the enemy is a master at?
faqs.answer: He says “all we need to do is be distracted… and the enemy of your soul is a master at this,” using “deception, doubt and temptation” to lure you from God.

faqs.question: What does he say about continually rebelling against God?
faqs.answer: He says “one thing you don’t do to God is continually rebel against him you’re not going to win,” and that “if you submit anyway you’ll be glad you did you becoming his slave actually makes you free.”

faqs.question: Why does he say Saul lost the throne?
faqs.answer: He says God would have “established your kingdom forever” through Saul, but “Saul didn’t have a heart for God,” and when told to wipe out a nation he spared the king and the best animals.

faqs.question: What does he say Solomon did wrong with his marriages?
faqs.answer: He says Israel had “been commanded by God… not to intermingle with the nations around them,” yet Solomon “let these women influence him and influence his heart,” and “the result was a disaster.”

faqs.question: Why does he say a ruler’s heart matters?
faqs.answer: He says “when a king turns his heart away from God… a lot of the people… will turn their heart away,” and “when the rulers were wicked a lot of the people were wicked.”
